finding: Retention allowed multiple distinct successor plans to share one predecessor, leaving an ambiguous resident continuation.
repair: After locking the predecessor, reject a new append when a successor is already retained. Exact replay is handled before this check. Replacement is not silently treated as append.

verification.negative_case: Existing successor rejects admission before checkpoint evidence lookup or INSERT.
verification.positive_case: Initial successor retention and exact replay remain accepted.

limitations: Controlled SQL fixtures do not prove real PostgreSQL concurrency isolation.
This guard relies on the existing transactional predecessor/goal locks and sole retention writer; it is not a database uniqueness constraint.
Replacement after cancellation requires its own explicit lifecycle, still unimplemented.
Resident successor delivery and handoff remain unimplemented. No EXE build or live Minecraft test ran.
